title: GraphCast Multi-Mesh GNN Surpasses Physics-Based Global Weather Forecasting in Under a Minute
aiSystem: GraphCast (Multi-Mesh Graph Neural Network — Google DeepMind)
whyItMatters: Beat ECMWF’s gold-standard physics weather simulator (HRES) on 90% of targets in under a minute on one TPU—ushering in operational AI meteorology worldwide.
summary: Published in Science in November 2023 by Remi Lam, Alvaro Sanchez-Gonzalez, Matthew Willson, Peter Wirnsberger, and the Google DeepMind team, GraphCast trained a multi-mesh graph neural network on 39 years of ERA5 atmospheric reanalysis to produce 10-day global 0.25° weather forecasts in under one minute on a single TPU—outperforming ECMWF’s operational HRES numerical solver on 90% of 1,380 verification targets and improving tropical cyclone track prediction. Its deterministic breakthrough directly enabled probabilistic diffusion successors such as GenCast (Nature, Dec 2024) and global operational AI weather suites.
technicalHighlights: Outperformed ECMWF’s gold-standard HRES physical solver on 90% of 1,380 atmospheric verification targets while running ~1,000× faster and more energy-efficiently.
Improved tracking of extreme weather including tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers, and extreme temperature anomalies without explicit PDE solvers.
Open-sourced weights and code, catalyzing operational ML weather adoption across ECMWF (AIFS), NOAA, and WeatherNext.
caveats: Produces deterministic point forecasts that blur fine-scale uncertainty at long lead times (later addressed by GenCast’s probabilistic diffusion ensemble) and relies on historical physics-based ERA5 reanalysis data.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that learned neural simulators can surpass decades of hand-crafted atmospheric PDE solvers on complex chaotic global fluid dynamics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Reshaped global weather agencies (ECMWF AIFS, NOAA, WeatherNext) and directly spawned probabilistic diffusion weather forecasting (GenCast).
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science (Nov 2023) with open-sourced code/weights and live operational verification by national meteorological agencies.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed multi-hour supercomputer numerical weather runs into <1 minute on a single accelerator.
